doc.title: Ed Soph interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 9, 2024

title: First paying gig and paying his way through school
summary: His first gig paid about fifty dollars, and he paid his own tuition with Dallas gigs at $60-75 a night.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: That’s what he meant. Do you remember what you made on your first paying gig?

Which was a lot of money back then, yeah. Yeah man, I paid my way through St. Thomas, paid my own tuition I’m proud to say, and I graduated from college without any student debt. Now that’s the other thing, these poor kids, man, that was — it wasn’t that, I’d say man I’d go to Dallas, I’d work seven nights a week when I was in school and making on the average $60 to $75 a night. My rent was $60 a month. I’d work one gig my rent was paid. And so yeah, there’s something to be said for those good old days. Because I’d drive to Dallas to play a gig, a jazz gig, a fun gig, and make damn near the same money I made when I was in school only maybe I make $75 instead of $60. Plus tips of course.
